name: Characteristic-p Yang Dimension
description: Family of Yang dimensions over a field of fixed positive characteristic $p$
definition: For each prime $p$, the **characteristic-$p$ Yang dimension** is $\mathrm{Y}_p(\mathcal H):=\operatorname{pd}_{\mathbb F_p}(I^*_{\mathcal H})$. Equivalently it is the regularity of the Yang complex over $\mathbb F_p$. Extension of scalars shows that it depends only on the characteristic, not on the particular field of characteristic $p$. For every prime $p$, $\mathrm Y_p\geq\mathrm Y_0$. For a fixed finite class, equality holds for all but finitely many primes; possible exceptional primes divide torsion in an integral homology group occurring in Hochster's formula. The Anchored Torsion Class has strictly larger Yang dimension in characteristic two than in characteristic zero or any odd characteristic. Thus characteristic dependence does occur. The Odd-Torsion Dual Class has the reverse strict inequality $\mathrm Y_3>\mathrm Y_2$. Thus neither characteristic two nor three dominates the other universally. These two finite examples do not establish unbounded-ratio incomparability or settle comparisons for every pair of positive primes.
graph_summary: Yang dimension over characteristic $p$, always at least $\mathrm Y_0$. Explicit finite classes give both $\mathrm Y_2>\mathrm Y_3$ and $\mathrm Y_3>\mathrm Y_2$.
comments: This database row is a uniformly quantified family, one parameter for each fixed prime $p$. Its $p=2$ specialization is the catalogue's default Yang dimension $\mathrm Y$. A direct lattice-homology census found $\mathrm Y_2=\mathrm Y_3$ for every class on at most four coordinates (up to cube symmetry); this is a bounded computation, not a general theorem.
origin_references: The underlying homological dimension was introduced by Yang in \cite{yang2018homological}; the coefficient-field notation is made explicit in the local Yang-dimension draft.

monotonic.proof: Yang's delta-versus-conjunction counterexample \cite{yang2018homological} has explicit cellular resolutions over an arbitrary field: on $2^d$ inputs the delta class has value $2^d-1$ and is contained in a conjunction class of value $d+1$. Thus monotonicity fails for every fixed positive characteristic when $d\geq3$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: Doubly monotonicity requires subfamily monotonicity, which is refuted by the recorded delta-versus-conjunction example.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires doubly monotonicity, which fails.

p_monotonic.proof: At a fixed coefficient field, restricting the domain (projection) cannot increase the projective dimension of Yang's canonical ideal.
